output.name: Sekar

anatomy.part: tusk tip, the far point of the straight spear
head, inside the melon forehead where the tusk springs from the brow
tail stock, at the narrow peduncle

output.myth: Sekar was a young one who wanted to go far north. He swam under the grey floes until the light turned blue. Orrun, who carries the islands on his back, felt the small one pass beneath him and said nothing, which for Orrun is a kind of blessing. At the top of the world Sekar came to the place where Hesk winds every string, and he pushed his head against the reel to see if it would give. It did not. The tusk came out of him then, straight and white, the way a bone comes through a bad knee. Aun saw it and laughed and cut a line to see what would happen. That is how the spear went up. The old ones say the tusk is only a tooth that got ideas. The young ones say it is the way north. Both are right, so both fly him on windy days.
output.verse:
Old ones say the tusk
is a tooth with ideas
young ones fly it north

problems: The blind guess ('a fish, head left, forked tail right') names the wrong category. The silhouette reads as a whale or dolphin, which appears only as the second alternative. The tall triangular dorsal fin (dorsal fin tip 113963 at about (353,210)) is what pushes the reading toward a fish or shark.
The figure is a real blue silhouette, not a copy of the gold lines. It is upright: dorsal fin on top, belly at the bottom, head on the left, flukes on the right.

Star placement is mostly sensible: tusk tip 1067 at about (84,206) sits at the far end of a straight gold line from head star 117020 at about (202,288), which suits 'straight spear'. Belly 115830 and low belly 115227 sit on the lower outline, and the flipper 116771 at about (214,364) sits under the head.
Head star 117020 sits on the outline edge rather than clearly inside the melon forehead. The melon bulge above the mouth line is not well defined.

Labels collide with the drawing and with each other: 'mid-back' overlaps the dorsal-side line, 'head, inside the melon forehead' runs over the back, 'flipper' is printed over its own star, and 'middle of the body' crosses the gold line and the tail-stock label. 'tail stock' and 'middle of the body' are nearly on top of each other.
The fluke pair is a small, narrow fork at the right end, not clearly two lobes spread horizontally, so the fluke-tip star 112029 at about (447,279) does not clearly mark an outer lobe.
The head/beak region is cramped: the tusk springs from the top of the head, but the outline has no visible beak or melon, so the narwhal identity is weak.
judge.advice: Redraw the silhouette so it reads unmistakably as a narwhal rather than a fish. (1) Head: give a rounded melon bulge at the front-top of the head, around (185-205, 255-290), with head star 117020 placed just inside that bulge at about (200,280) so the tusk springs from the brow. (2) Tusk: keep the straight gold line from 117020 to tusk tip 1067 at about (84,206), and make the outline itself follow it as a thin spear. (3) Dorsal: replace the tall triangular fin with a low, small ridge or hump near (345-355, 235-245), and move dorsal fin tip 113963 onto that hump, so the back line is smooth. (4) Back and mid-back: run the top outline smoothly from about (230,245) through back 115919 near (258,250) and mid-back 115444 near (282,256) to the hump. (5) Tail: narrow the peduncle so tail stock 112935 sits at about (400,295), then spread two distinct horizontal flukes, with outer-lobe tip 112029 at about (447,279) and the lower lobe near (450,312). Avoid a vertical forked fish tail. (6) Belly and flipper: keep the belly line through 115830 near (262,352) and low belly 115227 near (292,368); move the flipper 116771 to a small paddle at about (212,362) with a clear shape. (7) Labels: move each label to open space outside the silhouette with a short leader line, so none overlap gold lines or stars, and remove the 'mid-back' and 'flipper' collisions."]
